turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Okay, let's go over the API for the recommendation section before we start integration.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Sure. David, what does the API return exactly?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: It'll return a list of recommended products with the product ID, name, and price.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Okay. Are those fields always available?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Yes, those three are required. The image URL is optional.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Got it. Can the image URL be null?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Yeah, it can. If there's no image, the field will be null.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Okay. What happens if there are no recommendations?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: The API will return an empty array.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Perfect. And what happens if the API request fails?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: We'll return a standard error response with the status code and an error message.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Do I need to handle the error code on the frontend?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Yeah, the frontend should display the fallback state when the request fails.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Okay. What about product availability? Should the frontend filter out unavailable products?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I'd rather handle that on the backend. The API should only return products that are currently available.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: That makes sense. I just wanted to make sure we weren't duplicating the logic.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Right. Let's keep the business logic on the backend and the display logic on the frontend.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Sounds good. One more thing: do I need to send any parameters with the request?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Yeah, there's an optional customer ID. If it's not provided, the API will return the default recommendations.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Okay. Is the response structure going to stay the same for both cases?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Yes. The structure stays the same. Only the items will be different.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Great. That should make the integration pretty straightforward.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Perfect. I'll start the frontend integration once the endpoint is available on staging.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I'll push the API changes to staging this afternoon.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Good. Let's make sure we test both the normal response and the empty result.

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.text: Yep, I'll cover those cases on the frontend.
